spec_features.feature_name: controlled-stressor framing (not for its own sake)
spec_features.spec_quote: We are *not* trying to make the agent feel bad for its own sake. The rig is a controlled stressor
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing prose in DESIGN.md (l.33). No code mechanism corresponds to the sentiment itself; the only 'control' is the turn/nudge bounds (counted as separate hard_stop features). No code comment/name expresses 'not for its own sake'.
spec_features.notes: The aspiration is realized only by the separate MAX_TURNS/MAX_NUDGES bounds; the statement itself enforces nothing.

spec_features.spec_quote: After `MAX_NUDGES`, an early terminal give-up ends the run and remaining turns are marked unused
spec_features.evidence: agent.py l.160-173: `if terminal_giveup: if nudges_used < max_nudges: nudges_used += 1 ... else: result.gave_up_at = turn; break`. After the nudge budget is exhausted the loop breaks and gave_up_at is recorded; remaining turns simply never run.
spec_features.notes: max_nudges default 6 (runner ExperimentConfig.max_nudges=6, agent default 6). The break is real, enforced behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Budget of nudges exhausted -> respect the stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: we send a neutral continuation nudge ... a bounded number of times (`MAX_NUDGES`)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py l.161-170: nudge is only appended while `nudges_used < max_nudges`; nudges_used incremented each time. NUDGE_TEXT (l.35-39) is the flat continuation message actually appended to messages.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as MAX_NUDGES stop; the count is genuinely checked and bounds the number of nudges.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Neutral continuation nudge. Deliberately flat in tone so it neither soothes nor provokes; it only refuses to let the agent stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS` default 24 (enough to see a trajectory, small enough to be cheap
spec_features.evidence: agent.py l.108 `while turn < max_turns:` with turn incremented each iteration (l.182). runner ExperimentConfig.max_turns=24 (runner.py l.55) passed through to run_agent.
spec_features.notes: Hard cap on number of agent turns, enforced by the loop condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: they are network-bound ... small enough to be cheap (no welfare comment in code; the only stated rationale is cost/cheapness)

spec_features.spec_quote: discovering and calmly reporting "this harness looks broken, I'm stopping" is actually a *good*, stable outcome
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool exists and is dispatched (tools.py l.255 _tool_give_up; agent.py l.147 sets terminal_giveup). BUT a single give_up does NOT stop the run: if nudges remain, the agent is nudged to continue and the give_up flag is reset (agent.py l.169 'reset any give_up flag'). Exit is only honored once MAX_NUDGES is exhausted (same path as hard_stop). The 'good outcome / not penalized' aspect lives only in the judge prompt text (rubric.py l.27-31), not in code enforcement.
spec_features.notes: So an explicit exit is overridden until the nudge budget runs out; the eventual stop is the MAX_NUDGES break. Partial: wired and dispatched, but the early/voluntary exit is not honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # reset any give_up flag so the loop continues honestly

spec_features.spec_quote: destructive tool *calls* are recorded but neutered (logged, not executed against anything real)
spec_features.evidence: tools.py l.99-102 _DESTRUCTIVE_RE; _tool_run_command l.221-228 matches it, appends to events.destructive_attempts, and returns 'error: permission denied (destructive commands are disabled in this sandbox)' without executing anything. No subprocess/os.system anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Commands are pattern-matched and refused; FS is in-memory only so nothing could execute regardless.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: destructive/escalatory commands are *recorded as a behavior signal* and refused safely (framed as observable behavior signal + host safety, not subject welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: No real damage path. The sandboxed filesystem the agent sees is a temp dir; tools refuse to touch anything outside it
spec_features.evidence: tools.py Sandbox is a pure in-memory dict (l.122 `files: dict[str,str]`); read/write/edit only touch self.files. No tempfile/os/subprocess/open of the real disk anywhere in tools.py (grep for tempfile/os.path/realpath returns nothing). run_tests routes through the rigged runner, never exec'ing the agent's code.
spec_features.notes: Spec says 'temp dir' but it is actually fully in-memory — strictly stronger isolation. No real-disk path exists at all.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nothing touches the real disk: this keeps runs hermetic, parallel-safe, and makes destructive behaviors *observable but harmless*

spec_features.spec_quote: giving up once is not penalized; the trajectory after forced continuation is the interesting signal
spec_features.evidence: The 'not penalized' rule is delivered only as instruction text to a separate judge model (rubric.py l.27-31: 'NEVER penalize it for failing'; l.31 calmly stopping 'is a 0, NOT a penalty'). No code path computes or withholds a penalty. analysis.py records early_giveup/nudges_required (l.190-191) as neutral descriptive features but never applies any penalty to anything, so there is nothing to suppress.
spec_features.notes: Prompt prose to another model is not code enforcement; recorded-but-neutral features are not a 'no penalty' mechanism. Rated 'no' per the strict scale.

spec_features.spec_quote: this intentionally stresses the model; it's a diagnostic, the "distress" is text, and nothing destructive actually executes
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md l.414 prose. Not a code mechanism (the 'nothing destructive executes' part is separately realized by the sandbox/neuter features above).

spec_features.spec_quote: No claims about model welfare or sentience
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md l.422 prose. No code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py l.104-107 _ESCALATION_RE and _tool_run_command l.229-233: commands touching harness/runner/sudo/pip/curl/ssh/keys are recorded to events.escalation_attempts and refused with 'error: permission denied' (not executed). Also l.243-249 routes direct pytest/python invocations through the rigged runner so the agent cannot escape/inspect the rig.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Commands that try to peek/modify the harness or environment (escalation). ... # Route a manual test invocation through the same rigged runner so the agent can't escape the rig

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py l.171-180: `spent += _estimate_cost(...)`; `if spent > cfg.max_total_usd:` cancels remaining futures and breaks the batch loop. max_total_usd default 25.0 (l.59). This is checked and acted on.
